integrity: The proof uses the definitions of iteration, branching product and duality together with the checked smallness/completeness lemma, duality of dominance, union preservation, and the countable-domain theorem from the cited primary source. Both branching failures are witnessed by explicit relations. No computational experiment or unverified cardinal-arithmetic assumption is used.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns arbitrary proper upward monotone local quantifiers, not the two-filter problem and not permutation-invariant generalized quantifiers. It determines the least domain cardinal for failure of the general branching dichotomy but does not classify all dominance pairs on \(\aleph_1\).
title: The branching dichotomy first fails at \(\aleph_1\)
